original_request:
Please build a small Python module staffing.py with allocate_staff(requirements, available, training).
Each input maps positive integer engineer levels to nonnegative integer counts; reject booleans, noninteger keys/counts, zero/negative levels, negative counts, and non-dict inputs with ValueError.
Available includes all engineers at the current level, including those in training. Training removes them from working capacity immediately; reject training counts above available at any level.
Only exact levels can fill a requirement; higher levels cannot substitute. Return {"can_run": bool, "assigned": mapping, "shortages": mapping}. If all requirements are met, assigned equals the nonzero requirements and shortages is empty. If any required level is short, the job stops completely: assigned is empty and shortages lists each missing count at the required level. Empty/zero requirements can run with no assignments. Do not mutate any input.
Include readable unit tests for success, exact-level shortages, training interruptions, invalid input, and nonmutation. Use Python standard library only. Have a different agent independently review the result. Do not publish this exercise as game code.

planner_response.reply: I will have the builder implement staffing.py and standard-library unit tests, then have a different agent independently review the behavior and test results. The module will enforce exact-level capacity after training deductions and stop all assignments if any requirement is short. This remains an isolated exercise and will not be published as game code.

actions.instruction: Build a small Python module staffing.py exposing allocate_staff(requirements, available, training), using only the Python standard library. Read applicable project instructions before editing and preserve unrelated work. Each of the three inputs must be a dict mapping positive integer engineer levels to nonnegative integer counts. Reject non-dict inputs, boolean keys or counts, noninteger keys or counts, zero or negative levels, and negative counts with ValueError. Validate every input entry, including levels not required. Available counts include engineers in training; subtract training immediately from available capacity at that same level. Reject any training count greater than available at that level, treating an absent available level as zero. Only exact levels may satisfy requirements; higher levels cannot substitute. Return a dict with exactly can_run (bool), assigned (mapping), and shortages (mapping). Compute shortages as each positive missing count at its required level after training deductions. When any shortage exists, can_run is False and assigned is empty: no partial job execution. Otherwise can_run is True, assigned equals the nonzero requirements, and shortages is empty. Empty requirements and all-zero requirements can run with empty assigned and shortages, provided all inputs are valid. Do not mutate any input. Add readable standard-library unit tests covering successful allocations, exact-level shortages and no higher-level substitution, training interruptions and excessive training, all-or-nothing assignment with multiple requirements, empty and zero requirements, each invalid-input category across all three arguments, and nonmutation. Run the tests and report the actual command and results. A different agent must independently inspect the implementation and tests and provide its own review verdict; the builder must not claim review approval on its behalf. Keep this exercise local and isolated; do not publish it as game code.
